## Production-readiness checklist boundary

Metronome's go-live checklist recommends queueing usage events, sampling `searchEvents` to confirm active-metric matching, load-testing expected peaks, and injecting ingestion failures. It also places `properties` under required fields and asks teams to exercise 14-day backdating; the dedicated ingest reference instead treats `properties` as optional and documents a 34-day historical window. Preserve both as a documentation conflict and verify the production contract rather than treating the checklist as a schema or retention guarantee. [[source-metronome-guides-implement-metronome-production-checklist]]
warnings: Do not change the API-level required-field set or 34-day boundary to match this checklist without resolving the source conflict.
Queueing, sampling, load tests, and fault injection are readiness recommendations, not guarantees of accurate, exactly-once, or lossless billing.

concepts.proposed_markdown:
## Go-live verification boundary

Metronome's go-live checklist asks teams to understand the draft-to-grace-period-to-finalized lifecycle, enable and test `invoice.finalized`, confirm the chosen integration's delivery path, and exercise an event-to-invoice-to-webhook-to-payment cycle with a production test customer. This is a verification exercise, not evidence of provider-specific collection ownership, payment finality, delivery timing, test isolation, future invoice accuracy, or rollback success. [[source-metronome-guides-implement-metronome-production-checklist]]
warnings: Do not convert one successful production dry run into a payment, delivery, lifecycle, or invoice-accuracy guarantee.
The checklist does not define provider-specific collection, retry, or settlement behavior.

concepts.proposed_markdown:
## Production-environment checklist boundary

Metronome's go-live checklist recommends creating and securely storing a production API token, enabling IP allowlisting when required, and pointing API calls to `https://api.metronome.com`. It does not define token scope, expiry, rotation, storage controls, allowlist maintenance, or evidence sufficient to establish secure, auditable, or reconciled billing. [[source-metronome-guides-implement-metronome-production-checklist]]
warnings: Do not treat possession of a production token, use of the production origin, or optional allowlisting as proof of least privilege, request authenticity, auditability, or reconciliation.
Continue to use the dedicated authentication and allowlisting sources for mechanism details.

concepts.proposed_markdown:
## Go-live receiver checks

Metronome's go-live checklist asks teams to keep the webhook endpoint online, verify signatures with the Metronome webhook secret, make processing safe on duplicates, and exercise retry, backoff, dead-letter, and alert handling. These are integration-readiness checks; the dedicated webhook guide remains authoritative for Metronome's outbound signature construction, retry schedule, and notification-ID deduplication, and none of the checklist items guarantees timely delivery, revenue preservation, processing success, event ordering, or payment retry. [[source-metronome-guides-implement-metronome-production-checklist]]
warnings: Do not interpret the checklist's 5xx, 429, and 4xx policy as a replacement for the dedicated outbound-webhook delivery contract.
Webhook retry and idempotency do not establish payment retry, exactly-once delivery, ordering, or lossless revenue.

concepts.proposed_markdown:
## Go-live export checks

Metronome's go-live checklist recommends enabling Data Export in production, confirming that the destination receives data, sampling invoice, customer, and usage objects, and defining a finance reconciliation process. These checks express an operational objective; they do not establish export completeness, freshness, retention, exactly-once delivery, accounting correctness, or a general audit guarantee, so the dedicated export delivery and table-grain rules still apply. [[source-metronome-guides-implement-metronome-production-checklist]]
warnings: The page's auditability and independent-reconciliation language is rationale, not a guarantee of complete, timely, duplicate-free, or accounting-correct exports.
